findings.claim: carried-into-wave-5.md requires the value-parity requests, including the repeated-slash case /a//b, to reach a handler, but does not say this case needs the mergeSlashes policy. Under the strict default policy no route can match /a//b: RoutePattern.parse rejects a pattern with an empty interior segment and a :variable never matches an empty segment, and Router.decodeSegments keeps the empty segment unless policy.mergeSlashes() is set. A wave-5 implementer following the note under the default policy gets 404 and has no handler-side rawPath()/query() to compare, so the getPath() '//'-merging hazard stays untested. Round 3 W2-005 asked for '/a//b under the default and the mergeSlashes policy'; the note dropped the policy qualifier.
findings.suggested_fix: In carried-into-wave-5.md say that /a//b is sent with RouterPolicy.builder().mergeSlashes(true) (app.routerPolicy) to a /a/b route so it reaches the handler, and compare rawPath() (which must keep '//') across both adapters; under the strict default compare /a//b by status (404) only.

findings.claim: The 'Remaining markers' decision removes the routing.md markers for the TRACE/CONNECT setting API, the //-trailing-slash-case setting API and req.method() during automatic HEAD. The verified wave-2 test RoutingDocsTest.sdsAc10_OPS_ROUTE_001_AC3_wave1MarkersKeptAndNoneAdded asserts that routing.md holds exactly 4 marker lines, and that three of them are these markers. Its requirement OPS-ROUTE-001 AC-3 (verified) says they 'remain'. So the decided doc change makes a verified regression test fail. The wave design does not plan the SRS change or the test update. The project rule 'never weaken a test to reach green' and the sdd-only rule for editing body requirements leave the implementer without a sanctioned path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the decision: wave 3 supersedes or amends OPS-ROUTE-001 AC-3 through a guarded SRS mutation (wave-2 markers were kept 'for wave 3' by design). It also updates RoutingDocsTest to expect only the RouteBuilder use(middleware) marker, plus positive checks that routerPolicy/RouterPolicy and the HEAD value are documented.

findings.claim: Wave 3 fixes the Request signatures, which later waves may not change (I-014). Under D-072, method() returns a non-null Method (docs/api/request.md:11; routing.md switches on it in Java and Kotlin) and path() returns a non-null decoded path. Frozen D-117 has wave 4 run middleware on 'every request that reaches the dispatcher'. The unsupported-method 501 for an unknown token (for example BREW /x) reaches the dispatcher: D-422 asserts the dispatcher's 501 with an access-log line. So do the pre-lookup 400s for undecodable paths and OPTIONS *. For an unknown token there is no Method value to return, and for an undecodable path there is no decoded path. The wave design does not say whether these answers come before the middleware pipeline, or what method()/path() return for them. Wave 4 would then need either a nullable method() (an I-014 signature change) or an undocumented exemption from D-117.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a wave decision: the dispatcher answers the asterisk-form OPTIONS *, the non-'/' and validator 400s, the 400 for a malformed query (if it is meant to be included) and the unsupported-method 501 for a token that is not a Method constant before building a Request and before the D-117 pipeline. These requests still get the D-173 access-log line from the dispatcher's raw method token in wave 4. method() and path() stay @NonNull. Record the D-117 scope in carried notes for wave 4.

findings.claim: carried-into-wave-5.md requires the cross-adapter requests that compare rawPath() to reach a handler, including /a//b. Under the strict default policy /a//b reaches no handler. RoutePattern.parse rejects a pattern with an empty inner segment, and a :name variable never matches an empty segment, so the request ends in 404 and there is no rawPath() to compare. Likewise /a%20b can match only a variable pattern, because literal segments may not contain a space. The note does not name the routes or the policy that make these requests reach a handler.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the comparison app uses routerPolicy(RouterPolicy.builder().mergeSlashes(true).build()) for /a//b (or a separate app with that policy) and variable routes such as /:x and /:x/:y, so both requests reach a handler on both adapters.
